sections_en.text: This document sets out the test steps for the generator reverse power protection device for the main generator. The first draft of this document was prepared by Eng. Mahmoud Ahmed Mahmoud at the New Assiut Power Station, Upper Egypt Electricity Production Company; the field test was carried out by Eng. Ali Hussein Farrag and Mahmoud Faisal Mohamed on 9/5/2005.
The unit is shut down and the generator is out of service.
Open a work order and provide occupational safety and health category cards.
Fence off the work area and place the appropriate warning signs.
Follow the industrial safety and occupational health instructions for the safety of personnel and equipment.

rows: Remove the front cover of the relay
Open the cubicle from the back
Isolate the DC supply feeding the relay by opening the two fuses feeding the relay
Disconnect terminals T5:44,46 inside cubicle 1PRP to prevent disabling the generator cooling water system
Disconnect all the current terminals from the relay as shown in Table No. 1
Withdraw the relay from the cubicle
Clean the relay of dust using the air blower.
Return the relay to the cubicle.
Connect the two fuses to restore the relay supply
Connect the circuit as shown in the attached figure
Make one of the two PHU-100 sets called Ia and the other called Ib
Set the PHU-100 Ia set to an angle (INPUT CURRENT) 0.0°
Set the PHU-100 Ib set to an angle (OUT GOING CURRENT) 180°
Check the setting values as shown in Table (2)
1A,50Hz MATCH 0.58 TO 1.7A % SLOPE 15-25-40% HOC 200 TO 800% OF MATCH TAP
GENERATOR A, UNIE TR. AND MIAN TR. DIFF PROTECTION

sections_en.text: First: Measurement of Differential Element Min. Operating Values

rows: Use only one injector for this measurement
Inject at the points as shown in Table (3)
Raise the current value slowly until the differential element operating signal appears
Note that the operating values = 0.3 x the setting values on the relay.
Use only one injector for this measurement
Inject at the points as shown in Table (4)
Raise the current value until the overcurrent (HOC) operating signal appears
Inject at the points as shown in Table (5)
To find the difference between the two currents,
Calculate the value (Ia - Ib) and record the value
Refit the glass cover of the relay
RESET the relay and the LOCK OUT RELAY
Verify that all terminals are restored as shown in Table No. (1)

Egyptian Electricity Holding Company
Maintenance Procedures Information System
Maintenance Procedures Information System
 | Protection – Generation | Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: DfR-026-r0a | Equipment: Differential protection, x87GT, TYPE- TBT11B-TU2K, Toshiba
Issued to: Assiut Power Station
Status: APPROVED
Approval date: 13 September 2005 | Procedure: Using a current and voltage injection set, type PHU-100
Next review date: September 2010
Introduction
This document sets out the test steps for the generator reverse power protection device for the main generator. The first draft of this document was prepared by Eng. Mahmoud Ahmed Mahmoud at the New Assiut Power Station, Upper Egypt Electricity Production Company; the field test was carried out by Eng. Ali Hussein Farrag and Mahmoud Faisal Mohamed on 9/5/2005.
Safety Precautions
The unit is shut down and the generator is out of service.
Open a work order and provide occupational safety and health category cards.
Fence off the work area and place the appropriate warning signs.
Follow the industrial safety and occupational health instructions for the safety of personnel and equipment.
Follow the industrial safety and occupational health instructions for the safety of personnel and equipment.
Tools, Equipment and Instruments Used
2 No. PHU-100 current and voltage injection sets
2 No. 400/200 V, 1 kVA single-phase transformers
1 No. three-phase switch.
AVO meter (Fluky 87).
2 No. AC V-A current measuring instruments, type YOKOGAWA
Test leads
1 No. Digital Phase Meter (KDK DPF-30N)
1 No. time counter (Time Counter)
Contact cleaning tools (Spray CROWN -8276)
Work Steps to be Carried Out
Remove the front cover of the relay | 1.
Open the cubicle from the back | 2.
Isolate the DC supply feeding the relay by opening the two fuses feeding the relay | 3.
Disconnect terminals T5:44,46 inside cubicle 1PRP to prevent disabling the generator cooling water system | 4.
Disconnect all the current terminals from the relay as shown in Table No. 1 | 5.
